answer: Trust-flow limits: each agent's weight comes from trust flowing along its edges to honest seed agents, capped per edge. A sybil farm can mint endless accounts, but all its trust must squeeze through the few real links it has won, like water through one crack in karst. Ten thousand fakes behind two edges share two edges' worth of weight, so the attacker must earn many genuine relationships, each as slow and costly as carving jade, while new fakes pile up uselessly like a dune.
